title: Dedicated customer SLO dashboards (account/region) + access controls
creator: Aisha Bello
description:
Background
- Dedicated customers are asking for clear SLO/error budget reporting (Support: SUP-28412; follow-ups in SUP-28455).
- As part of Tiered SLOs + Error Budgets rollout, we need first-class dashboards that let SRE/CS/SE and (optionally) customer admins view account-level and region-level SLO status.
- Current “tiered SLO” dashboards are good for overall Hosted vs Dedicated but not per-account, and access is ad-hoc.

Goal
Deliver Dedicated customer SLO dashboards with correct SLI accounting and tight access controls:
1) Account-level overview: budget remaining, current burn rate, top failure/latency contributors.
2) Region-level breakdown: per region p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate, streaming reliability.
3) Endpoint class breakdown: chat/completions vs embeddings vs streaming.
4) Access controls: ensure only approved internal users (SRE/CS/SE) and/or customer tenant admins can view account dashboards.

Non-goals (this ticket)
- Changing the canonical SLI definitions (tracked under ENG-4921 / Confluence SLI spec).
- Private/VPC/on-prem dashboards.
- Fully generalized per-model/per-customer slicing for Hosted (cardinality risk).

References
- Confluence spec: eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tiered-slo-dashboards-and-alerts-spec
- SLI measurement standard: architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/sli-specification-api-gateway-and-routing
- Tier tagging ADR: adr-0142-tier-aware-sli-tagging-at-ingress (depends on ENG-4922)
- Burn rate approach ADR: adr-0143-error-budget-burn-rate-alerting-approach
- Observability pack PR (tiered baselines): observability-pack/pr-6312-tiered-slo-dashboards-and-annotations

Requirements / Acceptance criteria
Data correctness
- Dashboard queries must use tier-aware SLIs (Dedicated only) and match published SLI exclusion rules:
  - Exclude invalid requests (4xx), rate-limited (429), and client aborts (where we can confidently classify).
  - Streaming reliability: count server-side disconnect/error events; do not count client cancel/close as SLO failure.
- Latency measured end-to-end from gateway ingress to first-token (streaming) and completion (non-streaming), per SLI spec.

Views
- Dedicated Account Overview:
  - Error budget remaining (rolling 30d), budget burn over last 1h/6h/24h, and “budget state” badge (Green/Yellow/Red).
  - Success rate (30d) and latency SLO compliance status per endpoint class.
  - Top contributing regions/routes to error budget spend (last 24h / 7d).
  - Annotations: deploys + incidents (from incident-bot + deploy markers).
- Dedicated Account by Region:
  - Region table with success rate + latency percentiles + streaming disconnect rate.
  - Ability to filter to one region.
- Dedicated Account by Endpoint Class:
  - Chat/Completions, Embeddings, Streaming panels with relevant SLIs.

Access control
- Default: dashboards are internal-only; visible to SRE and limited CS/SE via explicit group membership.
- Account scoping: user must have access to that account’s dashboards; no “browse all accounts” for CS/SE by default.
- All access grants must be auditable (who granted, when, for what account).
- If/when we expose in Console to customers, enforce tenant isolation (no cross-account leakage) and follow existing Console RBAC patterns.

Cardinality / performance constraints
- Dedicated per-account metrics are acceptable but still need guardrails:
  - Use recording rules for per-account/per-region aggregates (not ad-hoc raw histogram scans).
  - No per-model breakdown by default; provide top-N breakdown only via precomputed series (or link-out to traces/logs).

Implementation plan (proposed)
1) Data sources
- Use tier + account tags propagated from ingress through routing:
  - Required labels: deployment_mode="dedicated", dedicated_account_id (or slug), region, endpoint_class, route.
- Use SLO config schema outputs (ENG-4926) + budget computation pipeline (ENG-4934) as the source of “budget remaining” and “budget state”.

2) Dashboarding surface
- Phase 1 (internal): Grafana folder “Dedicated / Customer SLOs” with templating by account + region.
- Phase 2 (customer-facing, follow-up): Console SLO page embeds the same aggregates via Dashboard API (separate ticket once Phase 1 is stable).

3) RBAC
- Grafana folder permissions:
  - SRE: admin
  - CS/SE: view (no edit)
  - Others: no access
- Account-level access:
  - Backed by an allowlist mapping (account_id -> groups) maintained in a small config repo / service.
  - Tie into existing internal access request flow (see INT-9331 pattern): request -> manager/owner approval -> group membership update.

Open questions
- Do we standardize on “dedicated_account_id” vs “customer_slug” as the metric label? (slug is nicer UX; id is safer). Proposal: store id as label; dashboard variable displays friendly name via lookup table.
- How do we want CS to share snapshots with customers (PDF export vs Console view)? Likely Console view later.

Deliverables
- Grafana dashboards:
  - Dedicated Account Overview
  - Dedicated Account / Region
  - Dedicated Account / Endpoint Class
- Recording rules / query library used by the dashboards.
- RBAC + access grant procedure documented (short runbook for CS/SRE).
- Validation checklist: compare at least 2 accounts against raw logs/traces for a known incident window and confirm numbers align.

Testing / Validation
- Pick two Dedicated accounts (one high volume, one low volume) and validate:
  - Success rate matches gateway 5xx excluding expected categories.
  - Streaming disconnect count matches event taxonomy.
  - Budget remaining changes in the expected direction during a replay of known burn window (use 2026-01-18 regression as a reference window, if tags exist).

Rollout
- Soft launch to SRE on-call first.
- Add CS/SE access only after access controls are verified and INT helpdesk flow is in place.
- Announce to CS via #support and update escalation playbook link.
comments: 2026-02-04 (Aisha Bello): Created from customer asks (SUP-28412) + program requirement. Felix to drive dashboard backend; Sergio to review Grafana patterns; Chloe to advise on future Console embed.

2026-02-06 (Felix Schneider): First pass of panel list drafted. Biggest risk is metric label availability for dedicated_account_id across fallback/routing. Blocking on ENG-4922 landing in prod + confirming tag propagation through streaming path.

2026-02-10 (Thomas Baird): Please avoid ad-hoc queries on raw histograms with account_id + route + region all at once. Recommend recording rules: per_account_region_endpoint_class aggregates only. Route breakdown should be top-N via separate pre-aggregation or link-out to tracing.

2026-02-12 (Sergio Costa): We can fork the tiered dashboards from observability-pack/pr-6312. Suggest folder structure: Dedicated/Customers/<account>. Need a clear story for templating vs dashboard-per-account to keep permissions manageable.

2026-02-14 (Rachel Kim): CS needs access that’s scoped to specific enterprise accounts; we cannot give broad “all accounts” access. Also need a repeatable access request template (timestamps, dashboard link, region). Referencing INT-9331.

2026-02-18 (Felix Schneider): Decided: single templated dashboard + account variable, but enforce access by provisioning separate Grafana folders per account with only that account variable pre-set (permissions at folder level). This avoids relying on Grafana variable security. Will document and keep automation minimal for first rollout.

2026-02-21 (Caleb Johnson): Confirmed dedicated_account_id is present on gateway metrics for non-streaming; streaming disconnect event series still missing tag in one code path (server-initiated close). Filed follow-up with Amara to patch instrumentation; not blocking initial dashboards if we clearly mark streaming reliability as “partial coverage” for affected regions.

2026-02-27 (Felix Schneider): In progress: dashboard JSONs drafted and tested against staging. Next: wire recording rules to reduce query latency; add annotations (deploy markers + incidents) and finalize RBAC runbook for CS/SRE.
